title: Letter 11 — The One Thing Needful, Once More
attribution_note: Letter 11 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: *“My brothers and friends!”*
You call me to come to you. And I had wished to come; but my infirmity, and the length of the road, and other reasons do not permit it. Forgive me, then, that I have stayed at home.
I desire for you, as for myself, salvation in Christ, for this *“is the one thing needful,”* in the Lord's own word [Luke 10:42].

Let the world love the things of the world; let some here seek honour, others glory, others treasure; let some care for the earth and their estates, and strive to leave their names upon their lands; let some build rich houses, gardens, galleries and ponds, and adorn their carriages and their horses, and furnish all the rest that serves for their own comfort — but to us, O Christians, our Christ sets before us “the one thing needful.”

What, then, is this? Eternal salvation; and He bids us seek it as “the one thing needful,” for without it there is no profit, though a man should have everything else. And whoever has eternal salvation has everything, though he lose everything else. In it is contained everything that could ever be desired. Without it the whole world is nothing, according to the word of the Lord: *“What is a man advantaged, if he gain the whole world, and lose himself, or be cast away”* [Matthew 16:26]? If the whole world is nothing, how much more is riches, however great; how much more is honour and glory, however loudly it resounds — for all riches, all honour and all glory are nothing against the whole world. And yet the whole world too is nothing, if the soul should lose its own treasure, eternal salvation. O how precious is eternal salvation! The whole world is nothing against it.

O how poor is that Christian who, having abandoned this priceless treasure, dearer than the whole world, seeks in this world to grow rich and to be glorified! Poor is such a man, and blind, and like one who, finding himself in a foreign country, and about soon to return to his own house and fatherland, should set about building there rich houses, gardens, ponds and other immovable things — all of which he must soon leave, and return to his fatherland with nothing. So, whoever, living in this world, gathers here, and does not *“grow rich toward God,”* to him God says: *“Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be which thou hast provided”* [Luke 12:20]? Whose shall your coffers of money be? Whose your houses? Whose your horses, your carriages, your gardens, your galleries, your ponds, your lands, your estates, your costly garments, and all your finery? For you, one grave is being made ready, and but a fathom of earth — and whither shall your glory and your honour, so dearly won, then depart? All will end, as your life itself will end.

sections.heading: A stranger building houses he must leave

pairs.en: *“When he dieth he shall carry nothing away: his glory shall not descend after him”* [Psalm 48:18]. Why, then, seek what is as nothing against salvation, and why chase after what departs from us like a shadow? We are sojourners and strangers on a foreign earth. Our fatherland is not here, O Christians! Why, then, do we gather treasures here, as though we were to live here for ever? Why do we not seek provision for our journey to our heavenly fatherland, but chase after what closes to us the very way to that fatherland?

Who would wish to have all the riches and glory of this world, and to be deprived of life? What profit is there in riches and glory without life? For life is dearer than all things. And if temporal life is dearer than all things, how much more is eternal life, against which even temporal life is nothing, and for whose sake even temporal life, when there is need, ought not to be spared. And if we abandon everything so as not to lose our temporal life, as happens in a fire, or in the invasion of enemies, and in other such straits, how much more ought we to abandon everything, so as not to lose the eternal.

He who strives to be rich and glorious upon the earth has no leisure to care for eternal life. *“For where”* his *“treasure”* is, *“there”* will his *“heart be also”* [Matthew 6:21]. Such care is a thorn, which chokes the seed of the Word of God, *“and it becometh unfruitful”* [Matthew 13:22]. Whoever wishes to obtain eternal life must receive the seed of the Word of God into his heart, and bring forth fruit. Therefore he must root out the thorn from his heart, that it may be free and fit to receive the seed of the Word of God. A vessel must be emptied, that it may be filled with something else; otherwise the one will not fit with the other — the heart, too, must be freed from excessive earthly cares, that the Word of God may find room in it. The love of riches, of honour, and of temporal glory must be driven out of the heart, if a man would let the holy Word of God into it, and bear fruit; otherwise the one will not fit with the other. Let us root out, then, beloved, the thorns of care for temporal honour, glory and riches from our hearts, and give room in them to the Word of God, that, dwelling in them, it may bring forth its own fruit — the fruit of true repentance, which God desires of us, and which the work of our salvation requires.

We have been called by God to eternal life, and renewed in holy Baptism for it; let us seek it alone with diligence, to which we have been called. It, once found, will never be lost; and, once lost, will never be found again. Honour, glory, riches, and the whole world, abandon us as we depart from here; but eternal life, once found, will be with us for ever.

Why do we seek riches, which will soon depart from us? God has promised us good things which *“eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man”* [1 Corinthians 2:9]. And they will be with us for ever and without change.

Why do we here seek honour and glory, which vanish like smoke? God has promised us eternal glory in the heavens, with which the glory of all the kings of this world cannot compare. Let us seek, then, this priceless and imperishable treasure. It “is the one thing needful.” Great and priceless is this treasure, for it was won for us *“not with corruptible things, as silver and gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot”* [1 Peter 1:18–19].

sections.heading: Behold the man, and his deeds

pairs.en: This treasure we had lost; but Christ has won it for us again by His own Blood, and gives it to those who truly repent and believe in Him. Let us seek it, then, by true repentance, which brings forth its own worthy fruits. Let us repent, then, that we may find it. For *“God hath said to the sinner: I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes”* [Psalm 49:21]. Hear this, ye sinners! God will reprove us, and set before our own eyes our sins, whatsoever we have ever committed, openly or in secret, in word, or in deed, or in thought. Let us repent, then, and blot out our sins with tears, that our sins may not be brought to light, and that none of us may then hear: “Behold the man, and his deeds!”

Behold a man, who was called a Christian, but did not do the deeds of a Christian. Behold a man, who *“had a form of godliness, but denied the power thereof”* [2 Timothy 3:5]. Behold a man, who *“professed that he knew God; but in works denied Him”* [Titus 1:16]. Behold a man, who promised at his Baptism to serve God, and bore the name of Christ upon him, but served the world, and served sin! For *“whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin,”* according to the word of the Lord [John 8:34]. Behold the man, and his deeds!

O how shameful and how dreadful it will be to hear this rebuke! From whom? From the Judge, God. To whom? To the Christian, who was called by the Christian name, but did the deeds of the pagans. For *“He shall rain snares upon sinners: fire and brimstone, and a stormy wind, is the portion of their cup”* [Psalm 10:6]. Let us repent, then, sinners, that this fate too may not overtake us. *“And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: every tree therefore which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire”* [Matthew 3:10]. Let us bring forth, beloved, the good fruits of repentance, that the Judgment of God may not cut us down as barren trees, and send us into the fire. Let us do this, that we too may not hear from the Judge, Christ: *“Depart from Me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels: for I was hungry, and ye gave Me no meat”* [Matthew 25:41–42].

O how dreadful it will be to hear this voice! Dreadful, too, to depart into everlasting fire, where *“the smoke of the torment of sinners ascendeth up for ever and ever”* [Revelation 14:11]; where *“their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched”* [Isaiah 66:24; Mark 9:44]; where *“men shall seek death, and shall not find it; and shall desire to die, and death shall flee from them”* [Revelation 9:6].

God even now awaits every man's repentance, not wishing that any should perish, for He is good, and loves mankind. Glory to His incomprehensible love for mankind! But the blind sinner, giving no thought to this, is careless, and strives to grow rich and to be glorified in the world, rather than to repent and be saved, and so to do the will of God.

O man! *“Or despisest thou the riches of His goodness and forbearance and longsuffering, not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?* *But after thy hardness and impenitent heart, thou treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God”* [Romans 2:4–5].

Let us turn, then, sinners, to God, while He waits for us; let us listen to Him, while He calls us. Let us cease to seek honour, glory and riches, for all this will depart from us; and let us seek that which will be with us for ever.

Now God calls us, and promises us His mercy; but soon He will call us, and will judge us. Now He says: “Repent” — but then He will say: “Answer Me!” Now He says: “Come unto Me” — but then He will say: “Depart from Me!” Now He listens to those who repent, and pray, and seek mercy of Him; but then, to those who repent and pray, He will answer: “I know you not” [Luke 13:27], since that will be the time of judgment and of testing, and not of repentance and of prayer. Let us repent, then, that we too may not hear: “I know you not.”

sections.heading: The day that comes like a thief

pairs.en: And near already is that dreadful day, and it will come unlooked for. *“And as it was in the days of Noe, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of man.* *They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.* *Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot: they did eat, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they builded; but the same day that Lot went out of Sodom, it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all: even thus shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed”* [Luke 16:26–30]. *“The day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night.* *For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them”* [1 Thessalonians 5:2–3]. In that day *“the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, and the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up”* [2 Peter 3:10]. Then, unlooked for, the cry will be heard: *“Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him”* [Matthew 25:6]. Then *“from His face the heaven and the earth shall flee away, and there shall be found no place for them”* [Revelation 20:11]. *“And the heaven departed as a scroll when it is rolled together; and every mountain and island were moved out of their places.* *And the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men, and every bondman, and every free man, hid themselves in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains; and said to the mountains and rocks, Fall on us, and hide us from the face of Him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: for the great day of His wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand”* [Revelation 6:14–17]?

Take heed, how dreadful that day will be for sinners, who now live without fear, and do not wish to repent. That same Christ, who for the sake of sinners lived in humility upon the earth, will then appear in Divine glory; and that same Christ, who *“was wounded for our transgressions, and bruised for our iniquities”* [Isaiah 53:5], will Himself judge the unrepentant sinners for their transgressions and their iniquities. If Christ suffered so greatly and so terribly for our sins, which He took upon Himself, satisfying the justice of God on our behalf, how fiercely will the wrath of God be kindled against sinners — and especially against Christians, who knew Christ who had come into the world, and confessed His name, but would not obey Him, and would not bring forth true repentance, and so be saved by His grace, but turned their hearts to the vanity of the world, and cared not for the salvation of their souls, but for the winning of honour, glory and riches, and walked after the desires of their own hearts — it is impossible to portray that wrath of God! Read the passages of Holy Scripture set down above, and consider them!

Let us turn, then, O Christians, from vanity, and repent, that we may not know the wrath of God upon ourselves, but may obtain His mercy, both here and there. Let us write the dread Judgment of Christ upon our minds, at which we must all appear. Dreadful and shameful it is for the guilty to stand at the judgment of men, and to hear the sentence of those present, and to be condemned by the laws, and to suffer punishment; every man avoids this. How much more dreadful will it be to stand at that dread judgment, where the Angels and all men who have ever lived since the creation of the world will be gathered, and to hear the sentence and the condemnation of God before all the world, and to be condemned to eternal punishment and torment with the devil and his evil angels. O God, spare us, Thine own creation!
The one who has truly repented will escape all this calamity, which I desire from my heart, both for you and for myself.

May the goodness of God move every sinner to repentance. Consider, O man, whose you are, whose work, whose creation and whose servant. You are God's creature and God's servant: *“Thy hands have made me and fashioned me”* [Psalm 118]. Why, then, do you not listen to your Creator, and honour Him? From whom do you receive every good thing, every day and every hour? From God. The bread you eat, the drink you drink, the clothing you wear, the fire that warms you and on which your food is cooked, the water with which you wash and cool yourself, the house in which you rest, the light by which you see, the air that keeps your life in you, the cattle that serve you, the estate with which you are content, and every other good thing you enjoy — whose is it? All of it is God's good gift. All this God gives you.

God gives you His own good things, and you do not honour Him! You honour and obey a human benefactor — your own father, say, your own master, your own ruler — but God, your highest Benefactor, your Lord, your Ruler and your Father, you will not honour and obey! For God cannot truly be honoured without the fear of God, and true repentance, and the keeping of His commandments. They are hypocrites who honour God with their lips only, to whom God says: *“This people draweth nigh unto Me with their mouth, and honoureth Me with their lips; but their heart is far from Me”* [Matthew 15:8]. God must be honoured not with the lips only, but with the heart also — that is, He must be feared, and loved, and His commandments kept with diligence. And above all, we ought to be moved to repentance, to obedience to Him, to love for Him, and to heartfelt thanksgiving, by His love for mankind — that for our sake, sinners, cast away, and perishing, *“He spared not His own Son, but delivered Him up for us all”* [Romans 8:32], that by His grace we might be saved. May this great and incomprehensible love of His for us make us wise, and turn us from the vanity of the world to Him, and to His love, and stir us up to heartfelt thanksgiving and obedience — without which we can do nothing that is pleasing to Him, whatever else we may do.
Be saved in Christ, and let one of you who fears God pray for me, a sinner.
